newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO says no appeal yet in bond case.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO says no appeal yet in bond case.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Thursday it had not yet appealed against a Dutch court's finding that it was liable for damages arising from a prospectus for bonds issued by failed German retailer Coop AG.
"We haven't filed for an appeal," ABN AMRO spokesman Jules Prast told Reuters, adding that the bank had until the end of this month to make a decision.

In August, an Amsterdam lower court ruled in favour of 80 investors who bought 200 million guilders of bonds issued by Coop in two issues lead managed by ABN AMRO in 1987 and 1988, a year before the German retailer collapsed.

Some investors who sold after the problems emerged lost money as the bonds plunged to 60 percent of their face value but most retained them and were repaid in full by Asko AG, which bought much of Coop's business.
The court found ABN AMRO responsible for the contents of the Coop prospectus, which assured investors of the group's financial health.
Lawyers acting for the bondholders have yet to specify the size of damages sought.
